stem:
Zara has a wooden cuboid with measurable length, width, and height. Amit has an irregular stone. Each needs the volume of their object. A measuring cylinder with water is available.

Which choice matches the correct volume method for each object?

options.text: Cuboid: length × width × height. Stone: final water reading minus initial water reading.
Cuboid: final water reading minus initial water reading. Stone: length × width × height.
Cuboid: length × width × height, even without measuring length, width, and height.
Both objects must use water displacement, because volume is found only that way.

teacher.key_rationale: A regular cuboid uses length × width × height after the three edges are measured. An irregular stone needs displacement: final minus initial water reading. Swapping methods, skipping edge measures, or forcing displacement for both is wrong.
